questions.context: Maria is at a park. She wants to throw away her plastic bottle. She says: "Excuse me, is there ___ recycling bin near here?" (She does not know of any particular bin.)
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct article.
questions.explanation: We mention a recycling bin for the first time and no specific one, so we use 'a' before the consonant sound.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: It's tempting, but 'the' points to a specific bin both people already know, and Maria doesn't know of one.
You use 'an' before a vowel sound, but 'recycling' starts with a consonant sound, so it's 'a'.

questions.context: A volunteer speaks on the phone: "I can't talk now. We ___ the river bank at the moment, and my hands are full." (clean)
questions.instruction: Fill in the blank with the correct form of the verb in brackets.
questions.explanation: 'At the moment' shows the action is happening right now, so we use the present continuous: 'are cleaning'.

commonWrongAnswers.comment: The simple present is for habits, but here the action is happening right now.
The past simple describes a finished action, but the volunteers are still cleaning now.
You need the -ing form after 'are' to make the present continuous.

questions.context: Last week, the landlord said that he will install solar panels.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: Last week, the landlord said that he would install solar panels.
questions.explanation: After the past verb 'said', reported 'will' usually changes to 'would', so it's 'would install'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: Last week, the landlord said that he wills install solar panels.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Modal verbs never take -s, so 'wills' is not a correct form.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: Last week, the landlord said that he would installed solar panels.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: After 'would' the verb stays in its base form, so 'install', not 'installed'.

questions.context: You should to bring your own bag when you go shopping.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: You should bring your own bag when you go shopping.
questions.explanation: After a modal like 'should', we use the bare verb without 'to', so it's 'should bring'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You should bringing your own bag when you go shopping.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: Modals are followed by the base form, not the -ing form.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You should to bring your own bag when you go shopping.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: This is the original sentence, and 'to' after 'should' is the mistake.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: You should brought your own bag when you go shopping.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: After 'should' you need the base form 'bring', not the past form.

questions.context: I avoid to drive to work because it pollutes the air.
questions.instruction: Rewrite the sentence with the error corrected.
questions.correctAnswer: I avoid driving to work because it pollutes the air.
questions.explanation: After 'avoid', the next verb takes -ing, so it's 'avoid driving'.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: I avoid drive to work because it pollutes the air.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You need the -ing form directly after 'avoid', so the bare verb 'drive' doesn't work.

commonWrongAnswers.answer: I avoid to driving to work because it pollutes the air.
commonWrongAnswers.comment: You've added -ing but kept 'to'; after 'avoid' just use 'driving'.
